input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: style() tests fg and bg for truthiness instead of `is not None`, so the 256-color index 0 is skipped
- failure path: click.style('x', fg=0) or bg=0, meaning black, applies no color at all and the text renders in the terminal default; the caller sees no error

Reviewer finding
- description: The truthiness check `if fg:` (and likewise `if bg:` at line 684) drops a valid color index of 0 (black in the 256-color palette), so style() silently emits no color code for it.
- rationale: Trigger: style('text', fg=0) or bg=0. The old check `is not None` included 0; the new `if fg:` treats 0 as false, so no escape code is added. Impact: black text or background is silently rendered in the default color, producing wrong output with no error.
critique: The finding pinpoints the same truthiness check on fg/bg in style(), which treats index 0 as false and skips the color. It gives the same silent no-color outcome.
